svg.text: ROOMS — SCALE COMPARISON BEFORE ANY DESIGN
Every Red Breach figure is measured. The Doom 3 envelope is a visual estimate off the reference screenshots, drawn as a band rather than a number.
ALL 22 FREIGHT ROOMS, THE CORRIDOR AND AN ESTIMATED DOOM 3 ROOM — ONE SCALE
THREE THINGS THIS SETTLES BEFORE WE DRAW ANYTHING
Doom 3's room language is a SMALL-room language.
Roughly ninety per cent of Doom 3 is corridor or very small room, and it has a known reputation
for little height variation. Our median freight room is around 1,600 m² — an order of magnitude
past anything in the reference. We can borrow its VOCABULARY and must not borrow its room
So the borrowed vocabulary is the part below 2.50 m.
Both reference shots show the same four moves: uprights at a rhythm dividing the wall into bays,
equipment set inside a bay rather than stuck on a flat wall, a floor plinth with a chamfered edge
defining a zone, and a ceiling mass centred on the thing below it. All of that is our corridor's
The real question is not the wall. It is the 40 m span.
A 6.00 m corridor opening into a 50 m room is a scale jump of nearly ten to one, and a 3.75 m
crown cannot carry it. `architecture-language.md` already names the answer — local ceiling planes,
service voids, enclosed pods inside a larger envelope — which is subdivision, not a bigger
A room wall is long enough to need the repetition rule too.
B4 has a 72 m wall and A4 a 66 m one, against a 52 m ceiling proven by walking it. Whatever
replaces the rib rhythm inside a room has to answer the same question the corridor did, and the
'structural bay' the language already names is the obvious candidate.
ROOM SCALE COMPARISON / paper only · Red Breach figures measured from the freight layout and the section module · Doom 3 envelope estimated from the reference screenshots, not measured from the game
